signatures.name: EICAR-Test-File
signatures.description: Standard antivirus industry test string (harmless, not malware).

signatures.name: WannaCry 2017 (documented sample hash)
signatures.description: SHA-256 of the widely documented WannaCry 2017 dropper sample.
signatures.source: public analyses: null0x4d5a (2017); 0xg4br (2023)

signatures.name: WannaCry (.wnry ransom-note paths)
signatures.description: Multilingual ransom-note template paths (msg/m_english.wnry) embedded in WannaCry binaries.
signatures.source: public analysis: alby0304/WannaCry_Analysis (embedded msg/*.wnry templates)

signatures.name: WannaCry (hardcoded killswitch domain)
signatures.description: Unregistered killswitch domain hardcoded in WannaCry; registering it stopped the 2017 outbreak.
signatures.source: Marcus Hutchins killswitch discovery (2017); 0xg4br (2023)

signatures.name: Petya / NotPetya (MBR ransom-note text)
signatures.description: Verbatim text from the Petya / NotPetya MBR ransom note.
signatures.pattern: If you see this text, then your files are no longer accessible, because they have been encrypted\.
signatures.source: public writeups of the Petya MBR note: secarma (2017); Barracuda (2017)

signatures.name: Ryuk (ransom-note sign-off / RyukReadMe)
signatures.description: Signature sign-off of Ryuk ransom notes and the RyukReadMe.txt/.html note filename.
signatures.source: FBI Flash Alert MC-000103-MW; ransomware.live; fourcore (2022)

signatures.name: LockBit (Restore-My-Files ransom note)
signatures.description: Filename of the ransom note dropped by every LockBit version (Restore-My-Files.txt).
signatures.source: SentinelOne LockBit 3.0 analysis; ACSC LockBit 3.0 profile (2023)

signatures.name: DoppelPaymer (Dridex-family code-reuse string)
signatures.description: Unicode string 'setup runn' copied verbatim across Dridex-family crimeware via lstrcpyW.
signatures.source: SentinelOne: code-reuse hunting across the Dridex family (DoppelPaymer / BitPaymer)

signatures.name: BitPaymer (wp_encrypt build string)
signatures.description: Build/config string 'wp_encrypt' found in BitPaymer (Everis extortion case) payloads.
signatures.source: SentinelOne: code-reuse hunting across the Dridex family

signatures.name: Stuxnet (OS-check code signature)
signatures.description: Byte signature of the Stuxnet OS-check routine (converted from the published TLP:WHITE YARA rule).
signatures.source: malpedia (Fkie-Fraunhofer CAAD), rule win_stuxnet_w1 by Silas Cutler, TLP:WHITE, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

signatures.name: Mirai (kills competing botnets hajime/anarchy/mozi)
signatures.description: Mirai binaries carry the list of competing botnets to kill (Hajime, Anarchy, Mozi).
signatures.source: original Mirai source release (2017); 'Understanding the Mirai Botnet', USENIX Security 2017

signatures.name: Mirai variant (2026 TBK/DVR campaign)
signatures.description: Campaign user-agent and firmware command trigger of the 2026 Mirai TBK/DVR wave.
signatures.source: ARMO Security Research, TLP:WHITE YARA rule (CVE-2024-3721 TBK DVR campaign)

signatures.name: Cobalt Strike (default named pipes)
signatures.description: Default named-pipe names used by Cobalt Strike beacons and post-exploitation tools.
signatures.source: Sigma rule 'Cobalt Strike Default Named Pipe' (TLP:WHITE); The DFIR Report (2021)

signatures.name: Cobalt Strike (default JA3/JARM TLS fingerprints)
signatures.description: Default JA3 (beacon/team-server) and JARM TLS fingerprints of unmodified Cobalt Strike.
signatures.source: public hunting guides: decryptiondigest (2026); t3l3m3try (2025)

signatures.name: Metasploit Meterpreter (ApacheBench PE template)
signatures.description: msfvenom .exe payloads are injected into an ApacheBench-based template that leaks its strings.
signatures.source: public analysis of the msfvenom default PE template (figurx, 2025)

signatures.name: Metasploit msfvenom (tool string in payloads/builds)
signatures.description: References to the msfvenom tool inside generated payloads or build artifacts.
signatures.source: documented msfvenom tool string in generated payloads / build artifacts

signatures.name: Emotet (documented sample hash)
signatures.description: SHA-256 of a documented Emotet binary. Real samples match by hash; Emotet's C2 rotates too fast for stable static IOCs.
signatures.source: NetScout ASERT 'Emotet - What's Changed?' (2020); CISA alert AA20-280A

signatures.name: TrickBot (documented sample hash)
signatures.description: SHA-256 of a documented TrickBot binary. Real samples match by hash.
signatures.source: NetScout ASERT 'Emotet - What's Changed?' (2020)

signatures.name: Dridex (leaked build PDB path)
signatures.description: PDB build path leaked inside Dridex loader executables (ASCII or UTF-16LE).
signatures.source: VK-Intel Dridex loader analysis + YARA signature (2018)

signatures.name: XMRig (miner CLI/config: donate-level)
signatures.description: XMRig command-line/config option. Dual-use tool, therefore flagged at medium severity.
signatures.source: XMRig public documentation + public miner-detection YARA rules

signatures.name: XMRig (default pool pool.minexmr.com)
signatures.description: Default XMRig pool URL appearing in miner binaries and configs.
signatures.source: XMRig public documentation (default example pool)

signatures.name: RedLine Stealer (documented XOR string key)
signatures.description: Hardcoded XOR key 'Raves' used by RedLine to obfuscate its strings. Short string, hence medium severity.
signatures.source: eSentire Threat Intelligence RedLine analysis (2024)
